data_note: Actual fitted forecasts on bundled synthetic retail history. Inventory quantities, costs and service targets below are explicitly chosen demonstration assumptions; they are not observed company business data.

recommendation.forecast_total_note: Sums of marginal quantiles are scenarios, not aggregate quantiles.
recommendation.demand_std_source: Sample standard deviation of observed historical demand
recommendation.probability_label: Fraction of sampled lead-time paths; model-based, not guaranteed.

sampling.method: Circular block bootstrap of centered, held-out forecast errors
sampling.assumptions: Errors remain representative of future demand. Blocks preserve local dependence only; block_size=1 assumes independent errors. Refits and pooled forecast leads limit calibration. Empirical tails cannot represent unseen extremes.

calculation_details: Base lead-time demand sums 7 period P50 values = 216.237 units. This median-based proxy is not an asserted mathematical expectation.
When triggered, order the largest of target-position gap, available EOQ, MOQ and one order multiple; round up to the multiple, then apply any inventory-position cap.
assumptions: On-order and backorders default to zero; MOQ defaults to no restriction and order multiple to one whole unit. Supplied values override these visible assumptions.
Analytical formulas assume independent demand across periods and independence of demand and lead time; historical variability may include trend/seasonality.
Lead-time quantiles come from aggregated sampled paths, never a sum of marginal P90s.
Risk and shortage scenarios use inventory position and assume on-order supply is available within lead time. Simulation uses explicit incoming-order arrival periods.
No profit margin, purchasing budget or cost value is invented. EOQ excludes shortages and assumes stationary annual demand and fixed order/holding costs.
recommendation.priority_rule: High risk first, then larger reorder-point deficit, then forecast volume.

deterministic_simulation.service_level_definition: Fraction of periods without newly unfilled demand
deterministic_simulation.cycle_note: Only complete receipt-to-receipt cycles; boundary cycles are excluded.
deterministic_simulation.turnover_note: Horizon COGS / average on-hand inventory value; requires supplied COGS and unit cost.
assumptions: Receive scheduled orders, clear old backorders, serve current demand, then review inventory position.
Static reorder point and target from the saved forecast; review once per observation period.
Orders beyond the horizon remain outstanding; no invented future demand or terminal costs.
Holding uses end-of-period on-hand stock and annual cost divided by frequency periods/year.
Ordering is charged once per placed order; shortage cost once per newly unfilled unit.
Purchasing costs and profit are excluded from total inventory operating cost.
A zero-demand path has fill rate 1 by convention; no completed cycles gives null cycle service.

sampling.method: Deterministic period P50 demand and fixed mean lead time

scenario.note: Both input sets are recalculated over the requested forecast horizon using the same saved forecast and simulation seed; no retraining. The saved plan is unchanged.

notes: Counts refer to SKU/location pairs. Monetary totals require complete costs and one shared currency; no currency conversion is assumed.
Target service level is a configuration, not measured achieved service.

Simulated totals require every current plan to have a simulation with matching forecast start, frequency, horizon, simulation and shortage modes; monetary sums also require a shared currency. Service means weight series equally. Portfolio cost percentiles are not inferred from marginal results.
ABC uses annual demand × supplied unit cost, sorted by value. Threshold-crossing items remain in their starting bucket; classification is among known values only.
XYZ uses historical sample standard deviation / mean. X<=0.5 and Y<=1 are configurable descriptive defaults, not universal business rules.
Zero mean or insufficient history is unclassified. Segments are context, not automatic business prescriptions.

benchmark.description: Isolated SQLite in-process HTTP benchmark; 1,000 synthetic locations reuse one actual 30-period forecast, 1,000 uncertainty paths each. No model retraining. This is not a 1,000-model training benchmark.
